fluff.overview:
The Naga is an 80-ton Clan assault OmniMech introduced in 2869 by Clan Wolf, born from the chassis of the Woodsman, itself the first heavy OmniMech produced by the Wolf Clan. When Clan Wolf technicians modified the Woodsman's torso to accommodate a pair of fixed Arrow IV artillery systems, the lateral extensions gave the design a distinctive silhouette resembling the hood of a mythological cobra, earning it the name Naga. In a warrior culture that prizes personal glory and ritual combat, a dedicated artillery platform was viewed by many as an abomination, yet the Naga's devastating performance at the Battle of Tukayyid silenced most critics and led to its adoption by several other Clans.

Manufacturing Plant WA3 on Arcadia produced the Naga until approximately 3085, when the remaining Homeworld Clans repurposed the production line for the Septicemia OmniMech. The design remains in limited service among the Spheroid Clans, though many surviving examples have been converted into the direct-fire focused Naga II.
fluff.capabilities:
The Naga was purpose-built to deliver sustained tactical artillery barrages while maintaining enough speed to reposition between volleys. Its pair of fixed Arrow IV artillery systems dominate the design, capable of firing homing rounds guided by TAG-equipped spotters or delivering indirect area-effect munitions. However, the sheer mass of these weapons systems consumes most of the available tonnage, leaving only 7.5 tons of pod space for secondary armament and ammunition. This severely limits the Naga's ability to defend itself at close range, a deliberate design choice that reinforces its role as a rear-echelon fire support platform.

Powered by a 400-rated XL fusion engine mounted on an endo steel frame, the Naga achieves a respectable top speed of 86 kph, making it one of the faster assault 'Mechs in any Clan touman. This mobility serves as the design's primary defensive asset, as the chassis mounts a meager nine tons of Forged Type 34 standard armor, woefully inadequate for an 80-ton machine engaged in direct combat. Twelve double heat sinks manage the modest thermal output.

In its Primary configuration, the Naga carries six tons of Arrow IV ammunition and three ER small lasers as its only close-range defense. All alternate configurations vary the balance between ammunition capacity and short-range firepower, reflecting the ongoing tension between sustained bombardment capability and self-preservation.
fluff.history:
The Naga traces its lineage to the Woodsman, Clan Wolf's first heavy OmniMech and one of the earliest attempts to develop modular BattleMech technology during the Golden Century. The Woodsman existed in two distinct development paths that would eventually produce three successor designs: the Timber Wolf and Gargoyle as direct combat replacements, and the Naga as a specialized artillery platform. When the first production run of the Woodsman proved to have technical issues, Clan Wolf technicians salvaged flawed chassis by extending the torso laterally to house Arrow IV systems. The resulting design first saw limited deployment in the mid-2900s.

The Naga spread slowly from Clan Wolf to other Clans, hampered by the warrior ethos that valued individual combat prowess over indirect fire support. Even Clans with relatively liberal combat doctrines did not widely accept the design until the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052, where the Naga proved its worth decisively. During the Wolf assault on Brzo and Skupo, Naga-equipped artillery Stars decimated ComStar's Tenth Army formations. After Skupo fell, Wolf Nagas continued to savage the retreating Com Guards, contributing to the capture of more than two hundred prisoners in that action alone.

The Naga's success at Tukayyid prompted wider adoption across Clan space. Clan Hell's Horses began fielding Naga-equipped artillery units soon after, followed by the Snow Ravens, Star Adders, Cloud Cobras, and even the Jade Falcons, though the latter deployed them in extremely limited numbers. Despite this proliferation, the Naga never entirely shed its reputation as an unglamorous assignment unsuitable for warriors seeking personal glory.

The Wars of Reaving brought an end to Naga production in the Kerensky Cluster. By 3085, the remaining Homeworld Clans had repurposed Manufacturing Plant WA3's production lines on Arcadia to build the Septicemia OmniMech, and Clan Goliath Scorpion took the last Homeworld Nagas with them when they were expelled from Clan space. Among the Spheroid Clans, the Jihad gave warriors a new appreciation for artillery assets, but also eroded the cultural taboo against assigning combat vehicles to front-line formations for fire support roles. With conventional artillery increasingly available, many surviving Nagas were converted into the direct-fire focused Naga II rather than maintained in their original configuration. Those Nagas that remain in service continue to fill their niche as potent artillery platforms, their Arrow IV systems still capable of reshaping a battlefield from beyond the reach of most return fire.
fluff.deployment: Alternate Configuration B is the most favored loadout among Naga pilots, carrying four tons of Arrow IV ammunition alongside an ER small laser and three ER medium lasers. This configuration strikes the best balance between artillery sustainability and personal defense, providing enough firepower to discourage light 'Mechs and battle armor from pressing attacks on isolated Nagas. The reduced ammunition supply demands more careful shot selection from the MechWarrior.
